title.narrative: Georgia Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to provide relief to micro, small, and medium-size enterprises and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance.

The development objective of Relief and Recovery for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Project for Georgia is to provide relief to micro, small, and medium-size enterprises and support their recovery, including by strengthening the enabling environment for access to finance. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Financial relief and recovery for MSMEs, has the following sub-components: (i) Grants for micro and small firms; (ii) Co-financing of interest payments; and (iii) Partial credit guarantees. 2) The second component, Digital payments and financial infrastructure upgrading, has the following sub-components: (i) Upgrading payments infrastructure; (ii) e-KYC and Know-Your-Customer registry; and (iii) Secured transactions reform. 3) The third component, Project management and monitoring, aims to finance the project management, implementation, and monitoring needs. 4) The fourth component, Contingency Emergency Response Component, is an unfunded contingency component that can be activated in case of a relevant emergency event.

title.narrative: Institutional actions to strengthen the partial credit guarantees program

baseline.value: EG currently does not have a monitoring system, a risk management framework, and an outreach strategy to evaluate the performance and risks of the program and propose improvements in its design.

target.value: EG has strengthened the design and implementation arrangements of the program, including more robust risk monitoring, awareness campaigns, stronger participation agreements with PFIs, and financial modelling tool.

comment.narrative: Institutional actions to strengthen the partial credit guarantee programs include: (1) introduction of measures to engage with PFIs, including the launch of an information and awareness campaign among PFIs, as well as the introduction of a risk monitoring system; (2) amendment of the participation agreements signed with PFIs to specify that EG can impose sanctions, remedies, and termination on PFIs; (3) adoption of a financial modelling tool.

actual.value: EG has (a) launched a campaign to share information and raise awareness among PFIs, (b) introduced a risk monitoring system for EG supported loans; (c) adopted a financial modelling tool; and (d) adopted amendments to the participation agreements signed with PFIs to specify that EG can impose sanctions, remedies, and termination on PFIs.

title.narrative: Institutional actions to strengthen the co-financing of interest payments program

baseline.value: EG does not have evaluation systems and measures in place to assess the effectiveness of its co-financing of interest payments on an frequent basis and better align its targeting towards strategic sectors and/or thematic areas.

target.value: EG has adopted a robust M&E framework and conducted an evaluation of its co-financing program, using evidence to propose amendments to improve targeting, eligibility criteria and other aspects of the program.

comment.narrative: Institutional actions to strengthen the co-financing of interest payments program include: (1) the adoption of a robust M&E framework, which improves the methodology for monitoring the impact of the program; (2) the completion of an evaluation of the co-financing program; (3) the amendments of the resolution governing the program to reflect improvements.

actual.value: (1) EG has developed and adopted a robust M&E framework; (2) EG has conducted an evaluation of its co-financing program; (3) amended a program to improve targeting.
